maria (eng-runtime): Heads up — we ran a shadow-traffic experiment yesterday that mixes replay + synthetic jitter against the embed/rerank endpoint. Posting initial notes and TL;DR: behavior suggests KV cache churn + large payloads cause 99.9p spikes when batch sizes and kernel selection interact.

sam (eng-ml): Can you dump the config used? particularly batch caps, kernel selection policy, and quantization settings.

maria (eng-runtime): Config snippet: `model: reranker-v2`, `kernel_policy: auto`, `batch_max_tokens: 8192`, `batch_max_requests: 64`, `quant: int4` for AVX nodes, `kv_cache_ttl: 30s` for the test. We also ran a second pass with `quant: int8` on the same hardware.

lee (eng-platform): How did you generate shadow traffic? replay or synthetic? any client-side pacing?

maria (eng-runtime): Hybrid: 70% replay (prod traces sampled to 0.5%) + 30% synthetic fanout to stress batching (Poisson arrivals, mean qps 1200, 95th burst to 2200). Added artificial payload sizes: small (1KB), medium (8KB), large (24KB).

ashley (eng-sre): Observed alerts? which metric spiked?

maria (eng-runtime): Alerts: tail-latency SLO trips on 99.9p for `rerank` route. Trace shows per-request latency jumping when payload >16KB AND kernel_policy selected "kernel-v2-fused-attn" (fallback in auto). CPU on host stayed low but GPU kernels showed queueing.

perf-bot: Profile summary: 1963456801 - peak qps 2320, 99.9p latency 1.8s (baseline 420ms). KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92% to 71% under burst.

sam (eng-ml): Interesting — KV hit-rate fall suggests embedding payload variance evicting prefixes. Are we batching across different vector dims?

maria (eng-runtime): All requests use same vector dim (512) but payload includes rerank metadata (doc snippets) that vary. Larger payloads increase sequence length, changing kernel decision and increasing memory for KV. Batching heuristic allowed mixing short and long sequences — that seems to push kernel selector to conservative fused kernels which are slower for our quantized path.

lee (eng-platform): Could we enforce batch homogeneity: group by seq_length_bucket at enqueue? Might reduce kernel flips mid-batch.

maria (eng-runtime): We tested bucketed batching (0-128,129-1024,1025+). Result: 99.9p improved 30% for medium bucket, but large bucket still had spikes due to eviction churn.

ashley (eng-sre): Any correlation with KV eviction policy? TTL 30s might be too low with our synthetic churn.

maria (eng-runtime): Yes. When we increased kv_cache_ttl to 5m for the run, hit-rate jumped to 89% and tail improved further, but memory consumption increased ~12% and we had a few OOM warnings on low-memory nodes.

sam (eng-ml): What about kernel selection override? force int8 kernel vs auto?

maria (eng-runtime): Forced int8 kernel reduced latency on large payloads by ~18% and reduced tail variance. However some microcases showed worse accuracy degradation (scoring delta ~0.6% on a small eval set). We need to weigh perf vs eval regression.

lee (eng-platform): Logs — posted a short snippet from the runtime when the spike happened:

```
[1963456812] queue_size=312 batch_requests=60 avg_seq_len=1187 selected_kernel=kernel-v2-fused-attn quant_mode=int4 kv_alloc_mb=8421 cache_hits=0.72
[1963456812] dispatch_latency=420ms kernel_exec=1.1s postproc=60ms total=1.58s
```

sam (eng-ml): The avg_seq_len=1187 explains the kernel choice. Fused-attn path isn't optimized for int4 on this hardware.

maria (eng-runtime): Actionable notes from runs: 1) Add seq_length_bucketed batching to enqueueer, 2) add soft batch_cap that prevents mixing >1024 with <256 in same batch, 3) bump kv_cache_ttl for rerank route in shadow to 2m to see mem/latency tradeoff, 4) expose kernel override knob per-route for canary.

lee (eng-platform): Also suggest improving kernel selector heuristic to prefer quant-friendly kernels when quant_mode detected and expected seq distribution >512. That would avoid fallback to fused-attn.

ashley (eng-sre): For load test reproducibility: please commit the exact synthetic traffic generator script + seed and the sampled replay trace ID to the perf repo. We need apples-to-apples for follow-ups.

maria (eng-runtime): Agreed — will push artifacts. Quick paste of the traffic-generator CLI we used:

```
./traffic-gen --replay-sample=projA:trace-2026-03 --replay-weight=0.7 --synthetic-weight=0.3 --seed=1729 --poisson-lambda=1200 --burst-scale=2.0 --payload-mix=1k:0.6,8k:0.3,24k:0.1
```

sam (eng-ml): Let's also run a controlled apples-to-apples with the same seeds but three kernel configs: `auto`, `force-int8-optimized`, `force-legacy` and capture p50/95/99/99.9 and KV hit-rate and memory.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll schedule the three runs on staging pool and post results. Also setting up an eval harness to check scoring delta for force-int8.

lee (eng-platform): Quick checklist for follow-ups: (a) add enqueue bucket logic PR, (b) kernel-selector tweak RFC, (c) traffic artifacts in perf repo, (d) run forced-int8 eval + perf. Who owns (a)-(d)?

maria (eng-runtime): I can owner (a) and run the tests.

sam (eng-ml): I'll take (d) and run the scoring regression checks.

lee (eng-platform): I'll prototype selector heuristic (b) and coordinate infra for runs.

ashley (eng-sre): I'll update runbook to include memory thresholds for kv_cache_ttl experiments and add alerts for cache_miss_rate spikes.

maria (eng-runtime): Cool — will post initial run artifacts and a short reproducibility doc by EOD tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Created perf ticket PERF-4983 with task list and linked artifacts.
